entries.description: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration, a division within the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS), today announced the Rare Disease Framework Initiative to reimagine the development of drugs and biologics for rare diseases.

entries.why_it_matters: RA teams across the industry should become aware of this new initiative as it may influence future regulatory expectations for rare disease products.

entries.why_it_matters: The RA team must ensure the sponsor completes the mandated studies and prepares documentation to meet the conditions for market authorization.

entries.label: WHO
entries.title: New WHO technical package to help countries improve health data for COVID-19 response and beyond
entries.description:
Today, as part of its commitment to strengthening health information systems and improving health[1], especially in the context of the COVID-19 pandemic, WHO announced a new approach to improving access to life-saving data: the SCORE for Health Data Technical Package. The COVID-19 pandemic has highlighted the urgent need for timely and reliable data to drive strategic health action. Too many countries still lack both the infrastructure to routinely gather health data and the analytical capacity to use these data for effective health actions and emergency response.

“Countries must be able to measure progress to make progress,” said WHO Director-General Dr Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus. “Particularly during COVID-19, reliable data is the best way to coordinate response efforts and improve health in all areas.”

Accurate health data are necessary to understand specific country needs in order to improve health and save lives. Data also helps direct scarce resources to where they are needed most.

The SCORE (Survey, Count, Optimize, Review, Enable) Technical Package aims to improve the availability of timely, reliable, validated, and comparable health data. For the first time in a single, harmonized package, it represents all the key elements for optimized health information system performance. Simply put, SCORE will help governments around the globe set benchmarks and i
entries.summary: WHO has released the SCORE for Health Data Technical Package to improve timely and reliable health data access.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams handling health data will need to incorporate the new framework to ensure compliance with improved data governance.

entries.label: FDA

entries.description: A U.S. Food and Drug Administration investigation resulted in a federal court order, dated Sept. 21, 2026, stopping a warehouse operator from distributing FDA-regulated products including food, drugs, medical devices, and cosmetics until it fixes its operations to meet federal legal requirements.

entries.why_it_matters: Regulatory affairs teams must ensure their products are not sourced from this operator until the court order is lifted, to avoid compliance violations.

entries.label: FDA

entries.description: The FDA today issued a direct final rule that updates its regulations to clarify that non-animal methods can be used where appropriate for testing the safety of drugs and biological products intended for human use before they’re tried in humans.
entries.summary: The FDA clarified that non-animal testing methods may be used for evaluating drug and biologic safety prior to human trials.
entries.why_it_matters: Regulatory affairs teams developing drugs and biologics must now consider non-animal methods in their safety studies and update protocols accordingly.
